title: Why Does Healing Take So Long for You?
paragraphs:
Why Does Healing Take So Long for You?
The silent war between your pain and God’s timing… and the grace you almost missed
You prayed for it to end.

You cried when no one was watching. You lifted your hands in worship while your heart was still breaking underneath. You told God you believed… but deep down, something in you whispered, “Why is this taking so long?”
And maybe you’ve been too afraid to say it out loud… but you’ve thought it.
“If God can heal instantly… why hasn’t He healed me yet?”
There’s a moment in Scripture that feels almost uncomfortable when you really slow down and sit inside it.
In Mark 8:23–25, Jesus heals a blind man—but not instantly.

“Καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ τυφλοῦ… ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν, Εἴ τι βλέπεις;”
(“Taking the blind man by the hand… He asked him, ‘Do you see anything?’”)

“Βλέπω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ὅτι ὡς δένδρα ὁρῶ περιπατοῦντας.”
(“I see people, but they look like trees walking.”)
Jesus touches him again… and then his sight is restored.
But don’t rush past that moment.
Jesus—the same Jesus who spoke and storms obeyed… the same Jesus who said “Lazarus, come out” and a dead man walked out of a grave—chose to heal this man in stages.
Because sometimes your healing is not delayed… it’s being developed.
You want instant clarity, but God is working through process.
You want relief, but God is building something deeper than relief—He’s building transformation.
The Hebrew word often used for healing is “רָפָא” (rapha)—not just meaning to cure, but to restore, to make whole, to mend what has been broken over time.
God is not just interested in stopping your pain.
He’s interested in restoring your soul.
But somewhere along the journey, the enemy starts whispering lies.
“If God loved you, this would be over by now.”
“If you had more faith, you’d already be healed.”
“If you were truly changed, you wouldn’t still struggle with this.”
But Scripture answers those lies with something deeper than emotion… it answers with truth.
“He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.”
The Hebrew paints a picture that feels almost too tender to ignore.

“הָרֹפֵא לִשְׁבוּרֵי־לֵב” (ha-rofe lishvurei-lev)
He is the healer of shattered hearts.
The kind of broken that takes time to piece back together.
And then it says He “binds up” their wounds.
Healing that takes time doesn’t mean God is distant.
Working deeper than you can see.
And maybe this is the part you didn’t expect to hear…
Some of you don’t actually want healing.
Because healing will require you to let go of things you’ve grown comfortable holding onto.
The Greek word for repentance is “μετάνοια” (metanoia)—a complete change of mind, direction, and inner life.
Because God isn’t just removing pain…
Even the version of yourself you’ve been clinging to.
So when you ask, “Why is this taking so long?”…
He answers, “Because I love you too much to heal you halfway.”
Half-healing wasn’t the end of the story.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.
But not fully clear yet either.
You’re walking… but it still hurts.
“He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion…”
The Greek word “ἐπιτελέσει” (epitelesei) means to finish, to bring to full completion, to perfect over time.
So no, your healing is not late.
But even Jesus, in the middle of suffering, cried out:

“Ἐλωΐ, Ἐλωΐ, λιμὰ σαβαχθανί?”
(“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”)
He understands what it feels like to be in the middle of pain that doesn’t immediately end.
The resurrection proved it was divine timing.
From what looked like the end… to eternal life.
So if your healing is taking longer than you expected…
Maybe it’s because God is writing something deeper than you imagined.
Something that won’t just change your circumstances…
This hit harder than you expected.
Your honesty might be the permission someone else needs to finally open up too.
And if you want to glorify God not just with words but with action… support what spreads His truth.
Follow closely if you’re done with shallow faith and ready for real transformation.
Because healing doesn’t just happen in moments.
It happens in what you choose daily.
Because the same God who started your healing…
Has already decided how your story ends.
And it doesn’t end in brokenness.
Your delay is not denial… it’s where God is rewriting you.
